result.stdout:
ytx extracts YouTube video metadata and captions as JSON.

Usage:
  ytx [options] <URL_OR_VIDEO_ID>
  echo '{"url":"URL_OR_VIDEO_ID"}' | ytx [options]

Arguments:
  URL_OR_VIDEO_ID           A YouTube URL or video ID. Put '--' before an ID
                            that starts with '-'. When given, piped input is
                            not read. Piped JSON uses only its "url" key.

Options:
  -u, --url <value>         Specify the YouTube URL or video ID explicitly.
  -l, --language <value>    Prefer captions matching a language name or code
                            (default: English). Falls back to English, then
                            any track, with a warning on stderr.
      --metadata-only       Skip caption retrieval and return metadata only.
  -f, --format <format>     json (default), or only the transcript as md, txt,
                            srt or vtt.
      --segments            Add a segments array of {start, end, text} to the
                            JSON, with times in seconds.
      --list-languages      List the video's caption tracks as JSON and exit.
      --proxy <url>         Send requests through this proxy, such as
                            http://host:8080 or socks5://host:1080. Without it,
                            HTTPS_PROXY and the system proxy are used.
      --timeout <seconds>   Give up after this many seconds (default: none).
  -c, --compact             Write compact JSON instead of indented JSON.
  -h, -?, --help            Show help and exit.
  -v, --version             Show the ytx version and exit.

Output:
  JSON (or the chosen format) is written to stdout. Diagnostics are written
  to stderr.

Exit codes:
  0  Success, including videos with no captions
  1  Video retrieval or another runtime error
  2  Invalid command-line usage or input
  3  Metadata written, but captions were blocked or failed
  130  Cancelled with Ctrl+C
